Bromotrifluoromethoxylation of allenes: expedient
access to allylic trifluoromethoxy derivatives†
Cite this: Org Chem Front , 2025,
Received 27th December 2024,
Accepted 21st March 2025
Rui Liu,<sup>a</sup> Yangdong Hou *<sup>b</sup> and Pingping Tang*<sup>a,b</sup>
rsc.li/frontiers-organic
A mild and eficient method for the bromotrifluoromethoxylation of allenes has been explored using trifl-
uoromethyl arylsulfonate (TFMS) as the trifluoromethoxy source. A series of allylic trifluoromethoxy
derivatives were obtained with high yields and good regioselectivity by terminal selectivity of the allenes.
This transition metal-free process expands the scope of the application of trifluoromethoxy reagents.
Introduction
The introduction of fluorinated functional groups into organic
molecules has a significant impact on their physical and
chemical properties.<sup>1</sup> Thus, more and more fluorinated drug
molecules are being synthesized.<sup>2</sup> In particular, the trifluoro-
methoxy group (OCF ) brings good metabolic stability and
high lipophilicity to molecules, earning it the nickname of
superhalogen.<sup>3</sup> The unique physical and chemical properties
of trifluoromethoxy functional groups have attracted attention
in the fields of materials science and pharmaceuticals.
However, the number of marketed drugs and agricultural
chemicals containing
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
remains low, and the study of

functional groups. Pioneering works have focused on the con-
struction of the

group, but this indirect method usually requires harsh con-
ditions or toxic reagents

Directly introdu-
cing an

functional group is an efective alternative
method for obtaining trifluoromethoxylated compounds.<sup>5</sup>
However, this is limited by the reversible decomposition of tri-
fluoromethoxy and trifluoromethoxylation reagents.
In 2017, our research group developed trifluoromethyl ben-
zenesulfonate (TFMS) as a trifluoromethoxy reagent, which
can be synthesized in one step from Togni reagent. It has been
used to achieve the first asymmetric trifluoromethoxylation
reaction, realizing internal trifluoromethoxylation selectivity of
alkenes (Scheme 1a).<sup>6</sup> Allenes exist in many natural products
and pharmaceuticals.<sup>7</sup> The high activity of allenes makes them
widely used as synthons for cyclization,<sup>8</sup> hydrogenheteroatom
reactions<sup>9</sup> and multifunctionalization.<sup>10</sup> With our continuous
eforts on the trifluoromethoxylation reactions,<sup>11</sup> we specu-
lated that if allenes were subjected to our reaction system,
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
would simultaneously be easily introduced into the pro-
ducts. However, the reaction of allenes presented more
complex reactivity than that of alkenes. The versatile reactiv-
ities of allenes allow for the selective modification of diferent
positions, enabling the synthesis of diferent regioselectivity
functionalized compounds,<sup>12</sup> which could deliver more poss-
ible trifluoromethoxylation products. This interesting but
questionable selectivity motivated us to investigate this chem-
istry. Conversely, due to the toxic reagents and the cost of tran-
sition metal catalysts or metallic reagents, transition metal-
free processes with readily available
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
sources have always
attracted the attention of chemists. Herein, we report our
eforts to develop a transition metal-free process for bromotri-
fluoromethoxylation of allenes with our trifluoromethoxy
reagent (Scheme 1b).

Results and discussion
To validate our hypothesis, the initial study focused on the
reaction of substrate 1a, which was treated with the previous
olefin reaction conditions. We were delighted to find the bro-
mosubstituted allyl trifluoromethoxy product 3a in 24% yield
with excellent regioselectivity but poor stereoselectivity (see
Table S1 in the ESI†). We did not detect the benzyl trifluoro-
methoxylation product, similar to the olefin reactions in our
previous work. Meanwhile, 3a was obtained in 11% yield
without the addition of silver fluoride and the ligand (Table 1,
entry 1). NBS delivered the product in 16% yield and resulted
in 56 : 44 E/Z selectivity. Other bromination reagents, such as
TBCA, PHBP, TBCO and N-bromosaccharin aforded the
desired product in less than 5% yield (Table 1, entries 3–6).
Further optimization of the bromination reagents revealed that
TBATB provided the best results, giving the corresponding
product 3a in 86% yield with 84 : 16 E/Z selectivity (Table 1,
entry 7). The product 3a was obtained with 76/24 E/Z selectivity
when using 2 equivalents of TBATB (Table 1, entry 8). 3a
cannot be obtained when using NaF or
\mathrm { C a F } _ { 2 } ,
perhaps due to
the poor solubility of these two fluoride salts (Table 1, entries
9 and 11). Otherwise, KF can aford 3a in 63% yield (Table 1,
entry 10). However, the yield significantly decreased to 27%
using silver fluoride (Table 1, entry 12). When the reaction was
performed at

reduced (Table 1, entry 13). Meanwhile, upon heating the reac-

To evaluate the practicability and eficiency of this reaction,
a gram-scale synthesis of 3a was conducted under the standard
reaction conditions in 73% yield (Scheme 3a). Further trans-
formation of the bromoallylic trifluoromethoxy products for
the construction of a series of OCF -containing compounds
was investigated (Scheme 3b). Under hydrogenation con-
ditions, alkyl trifluoromethoxy 5a can be obtained with a yield
of 61%. Propargyl trifluoromethoxy compound 5b was pro-
duced with a yield of 46% by eliminating hydrogen bromide.
To gain more insight into the reaction mechanism, we
carried out some control experiments (see Schemes S2 and S3
in the ESI†). Monitoring of the reaction between 1a and TBATB
by <sup>1</sup>H NMR spectrum showed that the characteristic hydrogen
of the allene has undergone a shift. The HRMS-ESI (m/z)
results indicated that alkene bromide ions were generated in
the reaction (Scheme 4). This indicates the appearance of bro-
monium active intermediates. Meanwhile, we also conducted
D-NOESY NMR spectra of 3a and 3d to confirm the configur-
ation (see Schemes S4–S6 in the ESI†).<sup>13</sup>

Conclusions
We have presented the first example of bromotrifluoromethox-
ylation of allenes using TFMS as an
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
source. By the com-
bination of TBATB with CsF, a transition metal-free process
with a readily available
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
source provided a range of allylic
trifluoromethoxy derivatives in up to 86% yield and with com-
plete regiocontrol, which are dificult to access by other
methods. Due to the easy decomposition of the
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
group,
carefully selecting the appropriate bromine source, reaction
temperature, solvent, and base were very critical, as all the
factors jointly guaranteed the smooth transformation. This
discovery also expanded the scope of the application of the tri-
fluoromethoxy reagent.
